cands.bio: Fourth-generation farmer and co-founder and chief executive of Hickory Nut Gap, a Fairview, NC sustainable meat business with about 25 employees. Graduated from Warren Wilson College. Had held no elected office before his 2026 run for North Carolina's 11th District.

endorsements.text: Endorsed by the Blue Dog PAC.

cands.gaps: We found no record of Ager holding any elected or appointed office, so there are no votes or official actions to report. His positions come from campaign material and a secondary summary. We found no stated position from him on homestead property taxes, foreign or investor ownership of land and homes, gun laws, abortion, school choice or teacher pay, or H-1B visas. His platform calls for comprehensive immigration reform without detailing enforcement measures. The data center moratorium is reported only in a Wikipedia summary, with no date or direct quote, and we could not find the original statement. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey. No controversies about him turned up in the pages we read.

The FEC's itemized file holds only $0 of their $106,192 in individual gifts so far, so where the money came from isn't shown.

cands.bio: Mortgage loan officer and small-business owner from Hendersonville who began in banking and finance in 1998. Elected to the North Carolina House (District 117, Henderson County) in 2022 and re-elected in 2024. Named the Republican nominee for U.S. House District 11 in August 2026.

endorsements.text: Donald Trump (R) is listed by Ballotpedia as endorsing her 2026 U.S. House campaign.

In her state House survey she listed endorsements from NC Values, the National Rifle Association, Americans for Prosperity, the National Federation of Independent Business, Stand For Health Freedom, North Carolina Grassroots Government PAC, North Carolina Property Rights Fund, Convention of States NC and North Carolina Right to Life. These are self-reported and were not confirmed with the groups.

cands.gaps: We could not find her stated or documented positions on data centers, homestead property taxes, immigration enforcement or H-1B, abortion, gun laws, school choice or teacher pay, or on growth and development. Ballotpedia's list of bills she sponsored was empty in the page we read, so we could not confirm any bill details. Her Candidate Connection answers are self-reported. We found no documented controversies, foreign ties or ties to foreign governments. We found no statements from her on a specific congressional platform beyond a campaign ad and a short bio.

local.label: Roots 100: Ballotpedia says she was born in Henderson County, and her campaign site says she grew up on her family's apple farm there and still lives in Hendersonville.

qual.background: Has worked in banking and finance since 1998 and is a mortgage loan officer and small-business owner. She has served in the North Carolina House since January 2023 and earned an associate degree in business administration, banking and finance in 2016.
qual.why: Three years as a state legislator plus long business and finance experience fits the middle range. There is no federal or executive office and no legal or prosecutorial background. Board and club service was not counted.
